findings.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every terminal. A field survey can start with the busiest terminals.
findings.what: 2 of 12 terminals don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
findings.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.

findings.effort: A default or per-trip field in your export.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_accessible on every trip. If every vehicle is accessible, this may be one default; otherwise use the value for each trip.
findings.what: 310 of 310 trips don't say whether the vehicle is wheelchair accessible.
findings.why: Even with accessible terminals, riders need to know the vessel itself can take them.

findings.effort: A small file for most flat-fare systems.
findings.fix: Add fare_attributes.txt (or Fares v2 files) with your fare structure. If your service is fare-free, ask to have it marked fare-free instead.
findings.what: The feed contains no fare information.
findings.why: Riders see 'fare unknown' in trip planners and can't budget their trip; visitors are most affected.

findings.effort: Usually one value per route pattern in your scheduling source.
findings.fix: Add the destination, direction, or 'via' label riders actually see to trip_headsign. Do not copy the route name. If the label changes during the trip, use stop_headsign.
findings.what: 51 of 310 trips lack rider-facing destination or direction text.
findings.why: When a route has multiple directions or patterns, the route name alone may not tell riders which service is coming.

findings.what: feed_info.txt has no technical contact (feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url).
findings.why: Trip-planning apps and regional data coordinators have nobody to email when they spot a problem with your feed, so problems linger.

completeness.name: completeness
completeness.summary: 83% of terminals state wheelchair accessibility (83% marked accessible, 0% marked not accessible). This measures what the feed publishes, not whether a terminal is physically usable. Fare data is not published.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'missing_timepoint_value' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Missing timepoint value (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: A few minutes per flagged trip.
findings.fix: Check the stop order and the shape direction in your scheduling software; the shape is often drawn backwards.
findings.what: On some trips the stops fall along the route line in a different order than the schedule lists.
findings.why: Trip planners can draw the vessel doubling back or skipping ahead, which confuses riders reading the map.

findings.effort: A few minutes per flagged terminal.
findings.fix: Check the flagged terminals' coordinates and the route shape in your scheduling software; re-snap whichever is misplaced.
findings.what: Some terminals sit far from the route line they belong to.
findings.why: Trip planners may draw the vessel route through the wrong path or point riders to the wrong terminal.

findings.effort: One field, set once in export settings.
findings.fix: Add feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url to feed_info.txt.
findings.what: feed_info.txt lists no contact email and no contact URL.
findings.why: Without a contact, apps like Google Maps can't reach you when they find a problem in the feed.

findings.effort: A field at a time; not urgent.
findings.fix: Review the flagged fields and fill in the ones your riders would use.
findings.what: Some files leave out fields that GTFS asks for but does not require.
findings.why: Recommended fields like agency_phone or stop descriptions make the feed more useful to riders and trip planners.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'same_name_and_description_for_stop' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Same name and description for stop (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'service_extends_far_in_the_future' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Service extends far in the future (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: Two fields in feed_info.txt, or one export setting.
findings.fix: Widen feed_start_date and feed_end_date to cover all service dates, or fix the dates that fall outside.
findings.what: Some service dates fall outside the date window set in feed_info.txt.
findings.why: feed_info.txt should span every day your service runs, so apps know when the data applies.
